title: Chapter 5: Introduction to Project Scope Management

questions.question: Which of the following best defines 'Scope' in project management?
options: Only the physical products produced by the project team
All the work involved in creating the project's products or services, as well as the processes used to build them
The financial budget and time constraints of the project
The documented list of team members and their responsibilities
questions.answer: All the work involved in creating the project's products or services, as well as the processes used to build them

questions.question: Project Scope Management ensures that the project includes:
options: As much work as possible to impress the client
All the work required, and ONLY the work required, to complete the project successfully
Only the work that the project team prefers to do
Additional features requested by external stakeholders during execution
questions.answer: All the work required, and ONLY the work required, to complete the project successfully

questions.question: Product Scope refers to what products or services the project will produce, whereas Project Scope refers to what processes will be used to build them.
How many distinct processes make up Project Scope Management?
Which two Project Scope Management processes belong to the Monitoring & Controlling (M&C) process group?
options: Plan Scope Management and Collect Requirements

questions.question: What is the core deliverable or output of the 'Define Scope' process?
What is the core deliverable or output of the 'Create WBS' process?
The 'Plan Scope Management' process utilizes which of the following as its main tools?
Which document describes how requirements will be collected, analyzed, prioritized, tracked, and managed across iterative cycles?
The PMBOK describes requirements as conditions or capabilities that must be met by the project or present in the product to satisfy an agreement.
Which requirements elicitation method involves shadowing users to see their actual operational workflows?
Comparing your project practices or product specs against industry best practices or competitors is a method known as:
Which method involves building mock-ups or working models to iterate user feedback?
What is a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)?
options: A financial model used to calculate ROI
A grid table linking product requirements from their origin to the deliverables that satisfy them
A visual diagram of the project team's hierarchy
A detailed technical manual for software installation
questions.answer: A grid table linking product requirements from their origin to the deliverables that satisfy them

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Project Scope Statement?
Clear statements in the Scope Statement regarding what IS NOT included in the project are designed to prevent:
How is 'Scope Creep' defined in project management?
options: The deliberate reduction of project scope to save money
The uncontrolled expansion of project scope without time or cost adjustments
The process of breaking down large tasks into smaller ones
The formal acceptance of completed deliverables
questions.answer: The uncontrolled expansion of project scope without time or cost adjustments

questions.question: The process of subdividing major project deliverables into smaller, more manageable components is known as:
What is the lowest level task entry in a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
Which document explains detailed specifics for each WBS code item, such as task responsibility, cost estimates, and resources needed?
The Scope Baseline is formed by combining which three documents?
options: Scope Management Plan + Gantt Chart + WBS

questions.question: Which approach to building a WBS involves reviewing a WBS from similar past projects and customizing it?
Which approach to building a WBS starts with the main project outcomes and decomposes downwards?
According to the 100% Rule, a unit of work must appear in only one place in the WBS, and the sum of child items equals 100% of the parent item.
In a WBS, a single item can have multiple individuals assigned with primary responsibility.
Project team members should be involved in developing the WBS to ensure consistency and team buy-in.
The process of formalizing acceptance of completed deliverables through customer inspection and sign-off is called:
During the 'Validate Scope' process, what happens if a customer inspects a deliverable and finds it unsatisfactory?
options: The Scope Baseline is permanently locked

questions.question: The primary mechanism used in 'Control Scope' to compare planned performance (Scope Baseline) against actual progress is called:
Which of the following is a key objective of the Control Scope process?
options: To collect initial requirements from stakeholders
To build mock-ups and working models
To ensure changes are processed through the Integrated Change Control system
To obtain formal sign-off on the final product
questions.answer: To ensure changes are processed through the Integrated Change Control system

questions.question: As a best practice to prevent scope problems, what does the acronym COTS stand for when advising teams to use existing technology before building custom solutions?
A best practice for scope management is maintaining 'Realism' by breaking large projects into smaller, more manageable ones.
Which software tool is most commonly used for creating WBS layouts and converting WBS tasks into Gantt Chart schedules?
Spreadsheets are often used in Scope Management for financial models, scoring matrices, and requirements traceability matrices.
